head: 339dd9f0a5c59fed2e40b550516bd50a2bf50ceb
summary:
HF-008 is fixed. Commit 339dd9f removes only the 30-line '# settled by SL-043' block from .taad/fitness.yaml (the diff is f8b98c4..339dd9f; everything else in it is slice ledger files). The three twinned entries at fitness.yaml:191-219 now cover these checks alone. They use the same file globs as the deleted entries and the same patterns plus a leading (?m). None of the patterns has a ^ or $ anchor, so (?m) changes nothing. They also set including_comments: true, so each is a strict superset of the entry it replaces. The App no-wait entry at :206-212 is untouched, and the contradicting line 'The App may wait on it' appears nowhere in the tree.

I planted one violation per SL-043 rule, plus one in the App, in a temp copy and ran the engine's own taad3.fitness.check on it.
- **Before (64 rules):** EntryClassifier.cs 2 hits, Scanner.cs 2, VolumeSpace.cs 3 (the third is a separate live-ScanStore rule), App 1.
- **After (61 rules):** 1, 1, 2 and 1.

So each violation is now reported once, and the App rule still catches a plant. On the real worktree the Fitness tool reports 61 rules and 'Every declared rule holds'. The full xUnit suite passed 400/400 with none skipped. rules-parity, RuleCases C-001, C-003 and C-007, and SettledCountProbe -Shape All all passed. The xUnit authority (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:128, :141-143 and :152-155) still enforces all three rules, with the App in scope at :141.

The slice has one build attempt and no loop. Contact is `code`: this is a rule-file change, and the checks ran the project's tools and the engine's rule checker on the tree and on copies of it. No device or live environment was involved, and none was needed.

checks.what: Diff of the build commit: only the settled SL-043 block is removed from fitness.yaml, and nothing else in the product or tests changes
checks.command: git diff f8b98c4 339dd9f --stat; git diff f8b98c4 339dd9f -- .taad/fitness.yaml
checks.evidence: fitness.yaml loses 30 lines: the '# settled by SL-043' comment plus the three entries (classifier link tags, nothing in Core waits, volume read cannot hold memory). The other files in the diff are .taad/slices/SL-074 ledger files.

checks.what: The twinned entries are strict supersets of the deleted ones
checks.evidence: The file globs are the same. The patterns are the same apart from a leading (?m), and none of them contains ^ or $. The twinned entries also set including_comments: true, which the settled ones did not. NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App) at :206-212 is intact.

checks.what: The contradicting 'App may wait' reason and the deleted rule names are gone from the tree
checks.command: git grep -n -i "App may wait|may wait on it|volume read cannot hold|classifier does not list link|nothing in Core waits" -- . ':!.taad/slices'
checks.evidence: Only fitness.yaml:204 (the twinned Core entry's reason), docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:148 and ScanStore.cs:65,72 match. All of them state the no-wait rule. None names or relies on the deleted entries, and none says the App may wait.

checks.what: Duplicate reporting is gone: one planted violation per SL-043 rule, plus one App plant, checked with the engine's taad3.fitness.check before and after the edit
checks.command: %TEMP%\sl074-validate-*\probe.py via C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Roaming\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe, engine root C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend, TAAD3_HOME in scratch; copies of src + before/after fitness.yaml
checks.evidence: before: rules=64, 8 violations. EntryClassifier.cs 2 (TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags + the settled copy), Scanner.cs 2 (NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) + 'nothing in Core waits'), VolumeSpace.cs 3 (TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore + the settled copy + 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore'), MainWindow.xaml.cs 1 (App). after: rules=61, 5 violations: 1, 1, 2 and 1, each SL-043 rule once. The clean copy after the edit had 0 violations. The 'unmatched' list and one unran import rule are the same before and after; they come from copying only src/. The temp folder was deleted afterwards.

checks.what: Engine Fitness on the actual worktree
checks.evidence: 61 rule(s) checked against 112 parsed file(s). Every declared rule holds.
Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 400, Skipped: 0, Total: 400, Duration: 23 s

checks.what: rules-parity between the yaml and the xUnit Facts
checks.evidence: rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 46 settled entries not compared. exit=0
All checks held. powershell.exe and pwsh both said 'AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 46 settled entries not compared'.

checks.what: RuleCases C-003 (new entry above or below the settled marker)
checks.evidence: All checks held. Above the marker: DRIFT 1 unpaired. Appended below: AGREE ... 47 settled.

checks.what: RuleCases C-007 (rules-harness against the real engine)
checks.evidence: All checks held. The clean scenario said 'xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits' and 'none unmatched'. The Fitness rule count equals twinned plus settled. The 1 import rule was named NOT RUN. A stray violation exits 2.

checks.what: The xUnit authority still enforces all three SL-043 rules, with the App in the no-wait scope
checks.evidence: :128 is the link-tag pattern. :141-143 are the no-wait patterns over src\FsAnalyser.Core and src\FsAnalyser.App. :152-155 is TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore with \bScanStore\b. All ran inside the 400/400 run.

checks.what: Loop check over the slice index
checks.evidence: One build attempt (caused_by null) and one code-review attempt. There were no send-backs, so there is no loop.

checks.what: Publishing and running the App exe
checks.evidence: The slice changes only .taad/fitness.yaml, a rule file read by the engine and by rules-parity. No product code changed, so the shipped exe cannot behave differently.

criteria.criterion: The three settled SL-043 entries that repeated TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags, NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) and TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore are deleted (or, if one stays, its reason is corrected)
criteria.how: git diff f8b98c4..339dd9f shows all three entries and their comment removed. The '# settled by' markers now run SL-042 then SL-044, with no SL-043.

criteria.criterion: Each violation of these rules is reported once, not twice
criteria.how: Planted-violation probe with the engine's taad3.fitness.check. Before the edit: 2, 2 and 3 hits. After: 1, 1 and 2. The remaining extra hit in VolumeSpace.cs is the separate 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' rule.

criteria.criterion: No text left in the tree says the App may wait on the volume figure
criteria.how: git grep for 'App may wait' / 'may wait on it' outside .taad/slices finds nothing. The App entry at fitness.yaml:206-212 and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:141 both forbid a wait in the App.

criteria.criterion: Enforcement does not weaken: the twinned entries are stricter supersets and the App no-wait rule still catches a violation
criteria.how: The globs and patterns are the same; (?m) has no effect without anchors; including_comments is true. The App plant was caught by NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App) before and after. The xUnit Facts still enforce all three.

criteria.criterion: The project's full test suite passes
criteria.how: eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx: 400 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

criteria.criterion: The rule tooling that counts or pairs yaml entries still agrees with the shorter yaml
criteria.how: rules-parity AGREE with 46 settled; RuleCases C-001, C-003 and C-007 and SettledCountProbe -Shape All all held; Fitness on the worktree: 61 rules, all hold.

not_reached: No test or guard stops a future slice from adding a settled entry that duplicates a twinned one; this regression path is open. The build recorded it as a follow-up, and it does not block this slice.
The before/after duplicate-report measurement came from a throwaway probe script in %TEMP%, deleted after use. Nothing in the repo pins HF-008's shape.
The App exe was not published or run. The slice changes no product code, so no environment beyond the rule checker and the test suite could show a difference.
